messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'gpool-7' queue length has exceeded threshold (current=62, threshold=20). Autoscaler attempted scale -> hit max_nodes=16. Multiple runtime Xid errors observed. Paging oncall.

alex: I’m looking. Latency & 429s starting to spike for a handful of customer routes. investig -> driver Xid spikes on nodes g-node-3g-5 / g-node-3g-6. :grimacing:

mira: @alex grabbing logs now. Any immediate SLO impact numbers?

alex: p95 token latency up from 120ms -> 900ms on affected shards. Error rate (500/502) from runtime up ~8% globally; real customer errors concentrated on these two pools.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident triggered - HIGH - infra_gpu_pool_exhaustion. Assigned to oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: Taking this. quick context?

alex: Autoscaler kept queuing requests; backlog hit queue_cooldown limit which triggered throttles. Autoscaler tried to provision more nodes but provisioner failed due to driver kernel panics on the new nodes (CUDA Xid 31/45). So available GPUs are lower than reported. We also saw OOMs in the runtime on the oldest node.

jamie: Adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-autoscale-exhaustion

leo: I see kube events showing repeated pod evictions on g-node-3g-6 with messages: "kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31" — suspect driver instability after recent kernel-driver update rolled last night.

mira: Can we shift traffic off gpool-7 to gpool-2 (stable) for critical routes? We should do a fast route-level fallback.

alex: Yes. Initiating routing override in gateway. Will route 3 critical customer routes to gpool-2. Expected improvement for them in ~30s.

ops-bot: ACTION: routing override created by alex -> route-ids [svc-a, svc-b, svc-c] -> target gpool-2. TTL=1h. :white_check_mark:

oncall-sre: Good. Next, we need to evacuate failing nodes and mark them unschedulable. @jamie can you coordinate node drain? Also need to disable autoscaling temporarily until we stabilize.

jamie: Running drain now: 
```
kubectl drain g-node-3g-6 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
kubectl drain g-node-3g-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
Eviction progressing, some pods evicting slowly due to long-lived connections.

leo: Telemetry: queue length for gpool-7 dropped ~40% post routing override. But autoscaler still shows active_nodes=14/16 and trying to create 2 more; AMI create calls failing with driver init timeout.

mira: On driver init errors — can we roll back last night's driver/kernel combo? Who owns that image?

alex: infra-image team deployed driver 525.60. Handle: infra-image@redwood. @mira ping infra-image for urgent rollback. We should also test reloading nvidia modules on the nodes before reprovisioning.

ops-bot: NOTE: Autoscaler disabled by oncall-sre (manual override) at 1769991250. Reason: avoid further provisioning of bad-image nodes.

oncall-sre: I’ve disabled autoscaler and started an automated health check that omits nodes created after 1769900000. Planning short-term fixes: 1) keep routing overrides for critical routes, 2) drain + reprovision affected nodes with previous driver, 3) notify customers if their traffic experienced errors >5%.

mira: Contacting infra-image now. Sending rollback request: "urgent: kernel-driver rollback for GPU image to previous stable (driver 520.xx). New nodes failing Xid on init." ETA from infra-image: 25-30m for rollback and new image publish.

jamie: While rollback inflight, we can try soft-restart of nvidia persistence on drained nodes (in case some recover) and then rejoin if stable. Command snippet for reference:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
```
Testing on g-node-3g-5 now.

leo: Log tail from g-node-3g-5 (recent):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=2456, ChannelId=0x2c
[ 1234.567895] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 9876 (runtime) total-vm:1234567kB
```

alex: OOMs show runtime is using a bad memory pattern under the new driver; draining may be safest. We'll reprovision with stable image only.

oncall-sre: Prepare customer impact statement. @mira can you draft a short blurb for support/sales? We need the affected customers, start time, steps taken, ETA for full remediation.

mira: Draft: "We experienced degraded inference availability for a subset of customers between 13:02 and ongoing UTC due to GPU capacity exhaustion caused by kernel/driver instability on newly provisioned nodes. We’ve routed critical traffic to stable pools, disabled autoscaling temporarily, drained affected nodes, and initiated a driver rollback. Estimated time to reprovision and restore normal autoscaling: 30-60 minutes. We’ll follow up with post-incident analysis." Thoughts?

jamie: Good. Add: "If you saw 5xxs please retry, and we’ll credit impacted token usage per policy."

alex: Notifying SRE infra and Sales ops to prep customer outreach for customers svc-a/svc-b/svc-c. Also create incident page.

ops-bot: INCIDENT: Created incident page https://incidents.redwood/1769991234 - owner: oncall-sre

leo: Infra-image replied: rollback image build started; publishing to AMI repo ETA ~28m. They also flagged a test failure on driver 525 with CUDA 12.1 that wasn't caught in staging.

oncall-sre: Once AMIs are ready, we'll reprovision drained nodes with stable image, join them back to gpool-7. Post-join, run smoke test and re-enable autoscaler in controlled mode (max_provision=2 over current nodes).

mira: For immediate mitigation, are there other quick config knobs? We could lower concurrency per worker to reduce memory pressure on remaining GPUs. That would reduce throughput but lower OOM chance.

alex: Agreed. Rolling per-worker concurrency from 8 -> 4 on gpool-2 (stable) and remaining nodes to reduce pressure. Implementing via config rollout now.

pagerduty-bot: Update: oncall-sre acknowledged. Severity remains HIGH.

jamie: Drain completed on g-node-3g-6. All critical pods rescheduled to gpool-2 & gpool-4. Starting reprovisioning steps only after AMI ready.

ops-bot: HEALTHCHECK: p95 latency for critical routes back to ~140ms after overrides & concurrency change. Error rate for those routes down to ~1.2%.

oncall-sre: Great. Next actions: - Keep routing overrides for 1h - Await AMI publish - Reprovision and rejoin nodes with stable driver - Re-enable autoscaler with stricter limits and an image-health gate - Postmortem and customer credits plan. Anyone opposed?

alex: no objections. Will monitor queues and telemetry closely. If anything worsens ping me directly.

mira: I’ll send the customer blurb to support/sales and post a short note on status page.

leo: Recording logs and preserving nodes for postmortem. Snapshotting g-node-3g-5 disk and capturing dmesg output.

oncall-sre: Thanks everyone. Handing off long tail to infra-image and platform-release. I’ll keep the incident page updated. If anyone needs to escalate to executive oncall, ping now.

ops-bot: NOTE: Autoscaler remains disabled. Manual re-enable pending verification. Next update at 1769991450 or earlier if changes.

alex: thanks all. :thumbsup:
